title: USO billets in Manila and Charles's gambling luck
summary: The USO troupe lives behind barbed wire in Manila, where Charles and Crack Stanley lose in the big crap games.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Anyway, we came back. And we spent several days down in Batangas, and back to Manilla. WE played in and around Manilla. We had a regular stage area where all the USO personnel lived. But everybody was billetted, men on one side of the barbed wire fence, and women on the other side. You come in at nights, you had a big gambling casino. And my brother, the great gambler, my brother, the great gambler, was always broke. He ain't never won nothing. He and Crack Stanley were supposed to have been two of the greatest St. Louis gamblers, they got over on there and they couldn't win a penny, and in the crap games, they were always five and six and seven thousand dollars in the game. Always, somebody was winning $1500 a night, $500 a night, and my poor little brother, bless his soul, he couldn't win a penny.
So we left Manilla -- what day was that, Charles?
That was in May -- I believe May the -- it was sometime in May.
